long_biography.plain_text:
Long before entering the fitness market, Lou Lentine learned to pair product design with selling. A University of Central Florida graduate, he appeared on home-shopping television while developing items that ranged from cleaning systems and electrical accessories to lighting. Patent filings made practical problem-solving a visible thread through the business he built.

That background shaped his move into technology-led exercise. Lentine launched Echelon around an affordable bike connected to digital classes, then widened it into hardware, applications and subscription content. He accepted outside growth capital without leaving leadership, and continues to work on device interfaces and training personalisation. The through-line is not a single invention but a repeatable process: devise, demonstrate and distribute.
